single_writer.next_pr: Nothing pending from this lane. If #407 ever changes its default, this matrix and the C++ derivation move in the same PR; tests/test_native_lease_default.py compares the two sources.
single_writer.closed: Closed 2026-10-28 without editing runtime/daemon.py. When --lease is absent the C++ Core derives $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/serveros/native-core.lease — the same path the daemon derives from XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. It is NOT byte-identical in the branch where the daemon falls back to its state root because XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset: there this Core has no equivalent root and REFUSES instead of inventing one, which preserves the invariant rather than the string. It also refuses when $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/serveros does not exist: the Core never creates it (the daemon does, for its status socket), so a fresh runtime directory is a loud refusal rather than a pass in which every unit is skipped for NO_LEASE. #407 has no change to make.

rename_complete_when: There is one binary named serverosd that performs bounded recovery, and no second program does — today bin/serverosd is Python and bin/serveros-native-core is C++, and both act.
The owner map still names exactly two owners; retiring one means retiring its gate sources with it, not renaming a directory.
scripts/build.py and scripts/release.py emit and verify the native payload as their own artifact kind (done for the release path in the native-runtime kind; the build face is not).
The Python daemon's bounded-recovery path is either gone or is a thin caller of the native one, with the tests that prove it.
